.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Dry and warmer through the week, possible rain on Sunday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
A highly amplified flow across the Lower 48 will feature a building
upper ridge over the mid section of the country expanding east 
through the week. This will result in dry weather and above 
normal temperatures through Saturday. The warming trend will be 
gradual as a subsidence inversion strengthens across the area 
limiting the depth of the mixed layer. 

The second half the weekend features a chance of rain as Pac 
energy moving into the mid and upper Mississippi Valley Sunday 
interacts with a southern branch system near the Southeast/Mid
Atlantic coast. GFS has been bouncing around from a more offshore
system to a low working straight up the eastern seaboard, like
the 00Z run, with a significant rainfall event Sunday in Sunday
night. The AI-GFS and EC-AIFS have been more consistent with 
bringing wet weather to the area then their operational counterparts,
but also have run to run issues with the magnitude of the low 
and track. Bottom line, the trend is up for rain chances Sunday,
but its not a lock. The interaction between the two streams 
will be key in whether this a more progressive offshore system, 
versus deeper and closer to the coast.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TUESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
High pressure in control through the TAF period. VFR prevails. 

Wind speeds will be closer to 10 kt this afternoon. The prevailing 
wind direction will be generally from the NW-W throughout the TAF 
period, with more of a NW component at times this afternoon in
comparison to Wednesday. Wind speeds tonight decrease to 5-7 kt at 
most city and coastal terminals, with light to calm winds for most
outlying terminals.    

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Wind directions could be off by 20-30 degrees from TAF at 
times this afternoon.

.OUTLOOK FOR 12Z Wednesday through Saturday... 

Wednesday: VFR. Winds W-WNW 5-8 kt.

Thursday-Saturday: VFR.

Sunday: Chance of MVFR or lower conditions developing in RA.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
High pressure will remain in control of the weather through the week 
with sub-SCA conditions. Winds will mostly  be from the NW-W at less 
than 15kt with seas on the ocean no higher than 2 to 3 ft.
